title: fix(ui): resolve linked automation runs beyond the first page
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: automation run links show unrelated recent history when the requested run is older than the first 50 entries.

## User Impact

User impact: automation message and notification links retrieve the exact recorded run, with **Show all runs** to return to normal paginated history. Linked runs ignore leftover history filters; ordinary job selection keeps those filters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing history query now receives the linked identity and resolves it before pagination. Public run IDs retain precedence; session and execution aliases must identify one run within the applicable scope. Existing visibility checks remain in place. The current Solid controller initializes the history selection before publishing the editor, and the UI renders that query-owned selection without a second highlight state.

## Evidence

The mounted current-main page and bundled browser both failed with the linked run behind 50 newer rows. The candidate opens the exact run, returns to 50 recent rows through **Show all runs**, and loads the older page. The original backend/query contract is unchanged by the Solid port.

![Before: linked automation opens unrelated recent history](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b834ea1-5a29-4ab7-847f-f495f352be78)

![After: the older linked run opens directly](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09688dc7-ed52-4393-bf3c-26cce901e5ad)

- `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/cron-job-link.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1 bundled browser scenario passed, 16.183 s wall; original current-main behavior failed in 19.543 s.
- `pnpm test ui/src/pages/cron/cron-page.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 26 tests passed, 5.688 s wall on the final Solid event-handler correction (earlier cost pass: 7.225 s). The existing linked-job table covers both inventory placements, older-run retrieval, stale filter clearing, **Show all runs**, and ordinary filter preservation.
- `pnpm test ui/src/lib/cron/refresh.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 33 tests passed, 3.221 s wall, including run-identity request and retained-page retirement.
- `pnpm test src/cron/run-history.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 10 tests passed, 8.681 s wall on the final assertion (cold first pass: 33.376 s). Cold compiled-worker preparation dominates the initial wall time; its existing worker/persistence cases verify durable history, while the added pure projection case protects public/session/execution identity precedence, collisions, scope, pagination, and visibility.
- Six focused UI owner/sibling files passed together: 131 tests, 10.184 s wall. The subsequent single-file cost pass covers the fixture-helper relocation.
- Production UI/core and owning UI-pages, UI-other, UI-e2e, and services-cron type graphs passed serially (54.932, 50.182, 54.497, 56.230, 46.783, and 36.435 s respectively). Conflict, line-cap, max-lines, assertion, test-mock, test-timeout, Lit, i18n, docs, formatting, and scoped style guards passed. Scoped typed lint passed in 13.965 s; fresh managed P2 review of the final candidate returned scoped-clean, with no actionable findings.

CI run 38143301565 passed at the published head in 559 seconds workflow wall time. UI jobs took 332, 279, and 280 seconds; bundled browser jobs took 116, 157, and 295 seconds. These are complete job durations, not per-file timings.

<details>
<summary>Validation failures and scope</summary>

The first port exposed Solid's synchronous editor-publication ordering: the linked history query was not initialized before recipient discovery published the new panel. Moving the existing query operation ahead of that publication fixed the two failing mounted cases; no duplicate selection state was added. A line-cap guard required moving the unchanged shared job fixture into the existing view test-support owner.

Typed lint caught a Promise-returning Solid click callback; explicitly discarding that promise matches the neighboring handlers and passed the final mounted replay and lint.

The first candidate browser run reached the exact linked run but its redundant final screenshot could not include the title after pagination scrolled it outside the viewport (37.821 s). The canonical full-frame screenshot is captured before the assertions; the redundant final capture was removed, and the complete scenario then passed. No sleeps, retries, longer timeouts, weakened assertions, or baseline exceptions were added.

The first managed review proposed resolving alias uniqueness after visibility filtering. We retained identity-first ambiguity: the link could intend the hidden record, so choosing a visible sibling would open the wrong run. Exact public IDs keep precedence, and the Gateway visibility collector retains its preparation contract. The existing projection scenario now asserts that a reused alias remains unavailable even when only one sibling passes the visibility filter (focused case: 10.264 s). The independent follow-up review accepted that rationale and returned scoped-clean; the final callback correction also passed a fresh scoped-clean review.

Earlier validation of the same backend/query contract recorded an unexplained signal-9 assertion-check interruption and an unexplained exit143 compiler interruption. Those historical attempts remain unclassified; the prior successful replays were not claimed to fix them. Fresh port validation is reported separately above.

Proof uses a synthetic mock Gateway. Live provider/channel delivery is not claimed. Reconnect selection preservation remains the independent follow-up in #169032; its integration must respect **Show all runs** retirement. No schema, permission, retention, protocol, or configuration contract is changed.
</details>
